title: Diversifiers and the regime de-risk overlay
hypothesis: A new uncorrelated sleeve or a risk overlay improves the book.
question: Is there any return stream left on this universe that diversifies the book, and does a simple regime rule cut drawdowns?
prior: Trend's worst losses cluster in sharp equity reversals; reacting to an observable regime is feasible even though predicting it is not.
citations: Moreira, A. & Muir, T. (2017). Volatility-Managed Portfolios. JF 72(4).
method: Screened cross-sectional ETF momentum and short-horizon reversal as sleeves.
Overlay grid: vol targeting, regime de-risk (halve exposure when SPY < 200-day average and 21-day vol > 20%), and both, on the base and meta books.
verdict_reason: The regime de-risk overlay passed: on the meta book it cut MaxDD from −10.5% to −5.4% and raised Sharpe 1.22 → 1.25; MaxDD stayed at −5.4% across every threshold perturbation. Both new sleeves failed (ETF momentum correlated 0.42 with the book; reversal lost money).
lessons: Return-stream diversification is exhausted on this universe; risk control was the last clean win.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
